# Create a task fork in one call

## Intent

An agent that starts a task needs its own disposable copy of a repository at once, whatever the size of that repository, and must not be able to disturb anyone else's work. Parley gives it a task fork: one call on a workspace returns a new workspace that is ready immediately, shares the parent's history without copying it, shows the parent's branches read-only and always current, takes the agent's work on branches of its own, and can come with a token that works only on that fork.

## Goals

- `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/forks` answers `201` with a fork in `status: "ready"`, its git remote URL and, when asked, a token bound to the fork and a sandbox; the fork is usable from that moment.
- Creating a fork writes no git object: the fork's repository holds no object and no pack after creation, and every commit reachable from the parent's branches and tags can be read through the fork.
- Every branch the parent has at creation appears in the fork as a tracking branch at the parent's current head, with no sync call; the parent's tags appear the same way; branches the agent creates belong to the fork alone.
- A caller who can only read a workspace can fork it and owns the fork.
- Every refusal of fork creation has one status and one `error_type`, and leaves nothing behind: no record, no repository directory, no token, no event.
- A fork refuses writes with `409 parent_archived` while its parent is archived and stays readable.
- `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/forks` lists a workspace's forks in pages, filtered by owner and by session.
- `parley fork create` and `parley fork list` drive the two routes from the shell.

## Requirements

### Creating a fork (WS-FR-067, WS-FR-069, §4.3.6)

`POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/forks` creates a task fork of the workspace `:slug`, the parent. A PAT needs the scope `workspaces:write`. Read access to the parent is enough: its owner and the members of its organization may fork (PLAT-FR-062). A token bound to the parent may fork it. The body is a JSON object in which every field is optional; an absent body and `{}` are valid, a member whose value is `null` counts as absent, and unknown fields are ignored.

| Field | Type | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | a generated id of 8 lower-case letters and digits | WS-FR-012: 1 to 32 characters; lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; starts and ends with a letter or digit; no `--` |
| `ref` | string | the parent's default branch | names a branch of the parent |
| `ttl` | duration | `[forks].default_ttl` (default `7d`) | WS-FR-013 form; at least 5 minutes and at most `[forks].max_ttl` (default `30d`) |
| `auto_change` | bool | `true` | |
| `token` | object | none | `{name?, permissions, paths?, expires?}` |
| `purpose` | string | `null` | at most 1024 characters |
| `session_id` | string | `null` | a UUID that satisfies the session-linking rule |
| `sandbox` | object | none | handed to the sandbox component |

The creation is synchronous. The answer is `201` with

```json
{ "workspace": { "…": "…" }, "remote": "<hub_url>", "token": { "…": "…" }, "sandbox": { "…": "…" } }
```

`workspace` is the fork's workspace object with `access: "owner"`. `remote` equals its `hub_url` (and is `null` when `[server].external_url` is not set). `token` and `sandbox` are present only when they were requested.

The fork is a workspace with: `slug` `<parent slug>--<name>`; `kind: "fork"`; `workspace_mode: "standard"`, also when the parent is a carry-patch workspace; `git_url`, `origin_head_sha`, `upstream_url`, `integration_branch` and `upstream_head_sha` `null`; `status: "ready"`; `owner_id` the caller's user id; `org_id` the parent's; `display_name` the slug; `description` `""`; `parent_slug`; `default_branch` equal to `ref`, the fork's base branch; `fork_point` `{ref, sha}`, the base branch and the parent's head of it at creation as a 40-character id, which never changes afterwards; `expires_at` the creation time plus `ttl`; `auto_change`, `purpose` and `session_id` as given or defaulted.

A generated name that is already in use is replaced by another generated name; the caller never sees a conflict for a name it did not choose (§4.10).

The call emits one hub event `parley.workspace.fork`, written with the fork (both are stored or neither): `workspace` and `resource_id` are the fork's slug, the actor is the caller, the event carries the fork's `session_id` when it has one, and its metadata is `parent_slug`, `fork_point`, `expires_at`, `auto_change`, `purpose` and, when a token was minted, `token_id`. A refused request emits no event.

The route accepts `Idempotency-Key` (PLAT-FR-015): a replay with the same key, caller and body within 24 hours answers `200` with the original body without the member `token.token`, and creates no second fork.

### Refusals of fork creation (WS-FR-006, WS-FR-007, WS-FR-061, WS-FR-072, §4.10)

Every refusal leaves the hub unchanged: no fork record, no repository directory, no token, no event.

| Case | Answer |
|---|---|
| the caller is the admin token (a fork needs a user as owner) | `403 forbidden` |
| the body is not a JSON object; `name` breaks WS-FR-012; `ref` is not a non-empty string; `ttl` is not a duration, is shorter than 5 minutes or longer than `[forks].max_ttl`; `auto_change` is not a boolean; `purpose` is not a string or is longer than 1024 characters; `token` or `sandbox` is not an object; `session_id` is not a UUID | `400 invalid_request` |
| `session_id` fails the session-linking rule | `400 unknown_session` |
| the parent is itself a fork | `400 not_supported_on_fork` |
| the parent is `pending` or `cloning`, or a reclone, archive or delete is running on it | `409 workspace_busy` |
| the parent is `failed` | `409 workspace_not_ready` |
| the parent is `archived` | `409 workspace_archived` |
| `ref` is not a branch of the parent: an unknown name, a tag or a commit id | `400`, `error_type` `fork_ref_not_found` |
| the parent already has `[forks].max_per_workspace` forks (default 200); deleted and expired forks do not count | `429 fork_limit_reached` |
| the given `name` is in use for this parent | `409 conflict` |
| the token is refused (below) | the token rules' answer |
| the sandbox component refuses | that component's answer |

When several cases hold, the answer is the first in the order of the table. Of two concurrent requests with the same `name`, exactly one answers `201` and the other `409 conflict`. Concurrent requests never bring a parent above its fork limit.

If the fork's repository or record cannot be written, the answer is `500 internal` and nothing remains.

### A token minted with the fork (WS-FR-076, PLAT-FR-081)

When the body has `token`, the hub creates, in the same step as the fork, a PAT owned by the caller and bound to the fork, and returns the `Token` object of §3 in `token`, with its secret in the member `token.token`. The secret is shown in this response only.

- `permissions` is a non-empty list of registered scopes.
- `paths` is an optional list of path globs that limits what the token may write.
- `expires` is an optional duration (WS-FR-013). With it, the token's `expires_at` is the creation time plus the duration. Without it, `expires_at` is `null` and the token lives as long as the fork.
- `name` defaults to `fork:<fork slug>`.

A `token` object that breaks these rules, or the token rules of §3 (an unregistered scope, an invalid glob), is `400 invalid_request`. If the caller authenticates with a PAT, it needs `tokens:manage` and must itself hold every requested scope, else `403 insufficient_scope`; if the caller's own PAT is path-limited, `paths` is required and each glob must be covered by one of the caller's, else `403 insufficient_scope`. In each of these cases no fork is created.

The hub records on the fork the id of the PAT that authenticated the request (nothing for an API key). A token bound to the parent therefore reaches the forks it created and no others.

### Session link and sandbox (WS-FR-077, WS-FR-082)

`session_id` is accepted when the session-linking rule of §14 holds for the caller and the parent: the session exists, was created by the caller's user, and its workspace is the parent or a fork of the parent. The session's status is not checked. The id is stored on the fork, shown in the fork's workspace object and carried on the fork's events. Otherwise the answer is `400 unknown_session`.

When the body has `sandbox`, the hub creates the fork and then hands the object, unread, to the sandbox component together with the caller, the fork, and the fork's `session_id` and `purpose` as defaults. The component's sandbox object is returned in `sandbox`. If the component refuses, the fork is not created either, and the answer is the component's error with its status, `error_type` and extra members unchanged. A hub without a sandbox component answers a request with `sandbox` `404`, `error_type` `sandboxes_disabled`.

### No copy (WS-FR-068, §4.3.6)

Creating a fork copies no history. After creation the fork's own repository holds no object and no pack, and the parent's repository is unchanged. Every commit reachable from the parent's branches and tags can be read through the fork at once, including commits the parent receives after the fork was created. What an agent writes to the fork is stored in the fork alone: an own branch and its new commits are not visible in the parent, and the storage a fork uses grows only with what is written to it.

### The fork's refs (§4.3.6, WS-FR-073, WS-FR-074, §4.10)

The hub gives every component that shows or serves a fork one view of its refs:

- **Tracking branches.** Every branch that exists in the parent when the fork is created is a tracking branch of the fork. Its head in the view is the parent's current head of the branch of the same name; when the parent's branch moves, the view moves with it. While the parent has no branch of that name, the tracking branch is absent from the view. Branches created in the parent later do not appear.
- **Tags.** The parent's tags that exist at creation are visible under the same rules.
- **Own branches.** Branches created in the fork, each marked as not tracking. A branch the parent creates later under a name the fork already uses changes nothing in the fork.

A tracking branch cannot be written in the fork: a component that asks whether a branch of a fork may be created, moved or deleted gets, for the name of a tracking branch, the refusal `403` with `error_type` `tracking_branch`, also while the parent has no branch of that name.

A fork's `head_sha` is the parent's current head of the fork's base branch, computed when the fork is read, and `null` when the parent no longer has that branch. `fork_point.sha` does not change.

### A fork follows its parent's status (WS-FR-066)

A fork is always `ready`. Components that act on a fork ask one check, with the kind of use:

| The parent | Read (fetch, API read) | Write (push, API write, update of the fork) |
|---|---|---|
| `ready` | allowed | allowed |
| `archived` | allowed | `409 parent_archived` |
| `pending` or `cloning`, or an archive or delete is running on it | `409 workspace_busy` | `409 workspace_busy` |
| `failed` | `409 workspace_not_ready` | `409 workspace_not_ready` |

Deleting a fork and its expiry are not subject to the check (package 16).

### Updating a fork's own fields (§4.5 `PATCH /workspaces/:slug`)

In an update of a fork, `purpose` takes a string of at most 1024 characters or `null`, which clears it, and `auto_change` takes a boolean. `auto_change: null`, a value of another type and a longer `purpose` are `400 invalid_request` and change nothing. The answer is `200` with the fork's workspace object; `parley.workspace.update` lists the given names in `metadata.fields` and carries the fork's `session_id`. Every update of a fork, of whichever field, is a write under the table above: `409 parent_archived` while the parent is archived.

### Listing forks (§4.5 `GET /workspaces/:slug/forks`)

`GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/forks` needs read access to `:slug` and, for a PAT, `workspaces:read` or `workspaces:write`. It answers `200` with `{"items": [workspace…], "next_cursor": …}`: the forks of the workspace as workspace objects with the caller's `access`, ordered by `created_at` descending, then `slug` ascending, with `limit` and `cursor` as on every list. `owner=me` keeps only the forks the caller owns. `session_id=<id>` keeps only the forks created with that session. Called with a fork's slug the list is empty. The list works in every status of the parent. For a workspace-bound token it holds only the forks the binding covers. An `owner` other than `me` and a `session_id` that is not a UUID are `400 invalid_request`.

### Fork limits in configuration (§4.9 `[forks]`, WS-FR-069, WS-FR-072)

| Key | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `[forks].default_ttl` | `7d` | a duration of at least 5 minutes |
| `[forks].max_ttl` | `30d` | a duration not shorter than `default_ttl` |
| `[forks].max_per_workspace` | `200` | the number of existing forks a parent may have |

A key that is omitted takes its default. A value that is not a duration, a `default_ttl` shorter than 5 minutes or a `max_ttl` shorter than `default_ttl` (equal is accepted) makes the configuration load fail with an error that names the key (`forks.default_ttl` or `forks.max_ttl`); `parleyd` then writes one error line and exits with status 1 without listening.

One rule judges every `ttl`: a positive whole number followed by one unit `m`, `h` or `d` (WS-FR-013), at least 5 minutes and at most `[forks].max_ttl`; `expires_at` is the given instant plus the `ttl`, in whole seconds UTC. Creation applies it with the creation time; package 16 applies the same rule with the request time when a `ttl` is updated.

### Commands (§4.6)

`parley fork create <parent>` calls `POST /workspaces/:slug/forks` and prints the response.

| Flag | Sent as |
|---|---|
| `--name <name>` | `name` |
| `--ref <branch>` | `ref` |
| `--ttl <duration>` | `ttl` |
| `--no-auto-change` | `auto_change: false` |
| `--token-permissions <list>` | `token.permissions`, split at commas; giving the flag is what requests a token |
| `--token-paths <globs>` | `token.paths`, split at commas |
| `--purpose <text>` | `purpose` |
| `--session <id>` | `session_id` |
| `--sandbox-profile <name>` | `sandbox.profile`; giving the flag is what requests a sandbox |
| `-- command...` | `sandbox.command`, the trailing arguments as a list |

A flag that is not given sends no member. `--token-paths` without `--token-permissions`, and a trailing command without `--sandbox-profile`, are usage errors: exit 2, nothing sent. When the response carries a token secret, the command says on stderr that it is printed this once only. Exit codes are 0, 1 and 2.

`parley fork list <parent>` calls `GET /workspaces/:slug/forks` with `--mine` (sends `owner=me`), `--session <id>`, `--limit` and `--cursor`, and prints the list page.

### End-to-end flows

1. **Fork with a token.** An agent runs `parley fork create demo --name task1 --token-permissions git:read,git:write`. The CLI posts to `parleyd`, which checks the caller, creates the fork's repository without copying an object, writes the fork, the bound token and the `parley.workspace.fork` event in one step and answers `201`. The CLI prints the fork, its remote and the token and warns on stderr. The agent reads the fork with the token; the same token gets `404` on another workspace. The developer who owns `demo` finds the fork with `parley fork list demo`.
2. **A member's fork follows the parent.** An org member who can only read `demo` posts to `/workspaces/demo/forks` and receives a fork they own. The parent's default branch then moves. `parleyd` shows the fork with the new `head_sha` and the old `fork_point.sha`, and the ref view shows the tracking branch at the parent's new head.

## Design Decisions

1. **Profile: full.** Two end-to-end flows cross the CLI, the router, the access component, the fork component, the store and git.
2. **Project-wide choices relied on.** Go; the hub runs the `git` command through `internal/gitrepo`, with no git library; repositories are bare repositories on disk; the store is embedded SQLite behind `internal/store`; HTTP is `net/http`; the CLI uses `github.com/spf13/cobra`; tests are table-driven with `testing` and `net/http/httptest`, on repositories made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`.
3. **How a fork shares history.** A fork's repository is an empty bare repository whose alternates file names the parent's object directory. Nothing is copied, later commits of the parent are readable at once, and what is pushed to the fork is stored in the fork. Its place comes from `internal/workspace`, like every copy.
4. **Tracking branches are names, not refs.** The fork's record keeps the names of the parent's branches and tags at creation; the ref view resolves them in the parent on every read. The fork's repository holds its own refs and, once it has been served over git, a copy of the tracking refs and of the version refs `refs/parley/changes/*` of its changes, which package 17 fetches from the parent before stock git runs; that copy is a cache and the ref view stays the one answer to which refs a fork has. Every own-branch listing of this package therefore leaves out the recorded tracking-branch names, so that a copied tracking ref is never shown as an own branch, also while the parent has no branch of that name. Recording the names costs time in the number of the parent's refs, not in its history; WS-FR-068 is read as speaking of history.
5. **A tracking name stays reserved.** While the parent has no branch of that name the tracking branch is absent, the name still cannot be used for an own branch, and the tracking branch is back when the parent has the branch again. The PRD says only that it disappears.
6. **Order of refusals** as in the table of "Refusals of fork creation". The PRD fixes validation before state (PLAT-FR-013) and is silent beyond that. `ref` is checked after the parent's state because the check reads the parent's repository. The token and the sandbox are created inside the fork's transaction, so their refusals come last and roll everything back.
7. **The admin token is refused at the access step**, before validation: `403 forbidden` whatever the body.
8. **Unknown body fields are ignored**, as in workspace creation (WS-FR-014), **and a `null` member counts as absent**, because `purpose` and `session_id` are shown as `null` and a client may send back what it read. The members of `token` are passed to the minting component of package 08, which validates them; `expires` is converted here to an instant.
9. **A token's `expires` may exceed the fork's `ttl`.** The token is revoked with the fork in any case.
10. **Session linking goes through the interface `SessionLinker`, declared in `internal/fork`** with two operations: a check (caller, session id, parent slug; accepted with the lower-case id, refused or failed) and a record (the fork's open transaction, the session id, the parent's slug and the fork's slug). Package 49 registers its `session.Check` and `session.Record` with it from `internal/hub/session.go` (link kind `fork`); this package does not depend on package 49. The check is called at fork creation, at its place in the order of refusals; the record is called inside the creation transaction, so the link is stored with the fork or not at all. Without a registered linker every `session_id` is `400 unknown_session`, because no session exists.
11. **The sandbox is asked through a narrow interface**, called once inside the fork's transaction after the fork and its token are written and the fork's repository exists. Package 45 registers its component from `internal/hub/sandbox.go`; without one the answer is `404 sandboxes_disabled`. The `sandboxes:write` scope of WS-FR-082 is checked by that component with the rest of the sandbox request, so that the answer is "the sandbox route's error".
12. **A generated name is tried at most 8 times**; after that the answer is `500 internal`. With 36^8 names this is not reached in practice, and a loop needs a bound.
13. **Leftovers.** The repository directory is made before the transaction and removed when the transaction fails. A directory found at a new fork's place with no fork record is discarded and replaced.
14. **`remote` is `null` when `[server].external_url` is not set**, like `hub_url`.
15. **A `failed` parent** makes the fork answer `409 workspace_not_ready`, as WS-FR-007 does for the workspace itself; WS-FR-066 names only `archived` and busy.
16. **The list of forks holds, for a bound token, only the forks its binding covers**, so that it never shows a workspace that then answers `404`. An admin token with `owner=me` gets an empty list.
17. **Lengths count Unicode code points**, as in package 11.
18. **`purpose` and `auto_change` in an update** go through package 11's update handler, which is a dependency: this package registers their handlers with `RegisterForkField` and the parent-state check with `RegisterForkUpdateGuard`, and edits no file of package 11. In `metadata.fields` they come last in package 11's fixed order (`display_name`, `description`, `org_id`, `settings`, `ttl`, `purpose`, `auto_change`).
19. **The lifetime at creation is this package's; extension, expiry and early removal are package 16's.** This package registers `[forks].default_ttl`, `[forks].max_ttl` and `[forks].max_per_workspace`, refuses a contradictory configuration, and owns `ResolveTTL` in `internal/fork/lifetime.go`, the one rule for a `ttl`, which sets `expires_at` at creation. Package 16 calls `ResolveTTL` for `ttl` in `PATCH` (WS-FR-071) and owns `[forks].expire_on_land`. Why here: creation needs the default and the bounds, and this package is built first.
20. **The fork view.** A fork's computed `head_sha` reaches the workspace object through `RegisterForkView` of package 10's `RenderWorkspace`.
21. **Composition.** The fork component and its optional collaborators are wired on the composition value of `internal/hub` (package 03), in `internal/hub/fork.go`; nothing is wired in `cmd/parleyd`.
22. **The fork token is minted only through `MintBound` of package 08.** The create handler calls `MintBound(ctx, tx, input)` of `internal/access` with the fork's transaction, the caller as owner, the authenticating credential as creator and the fork's slug as the binding. It never calls the minting operation of package 06 directly and writes no token row and no `parley.token.bind` event itself; validation of permissions, paths and expiry, the subset rule and that event are `MintBound`'s, and its API error is answered unchanged.

## Dependencies

- Package 10 workspace_create_and_clone (draft): the workspace store and record, the fork-name and duration validators, the state guard and maintenance marker, the place of a repository copy, the workspace object, the `git` wrapper and the event component as it uses it.
- Package 08 workspace_bound_tokens (draft): `MintBound`, the minting component that creates the fork-bound token inside the fork's transaction, the creating-token field on the workspace record, and the guard that lets a token bound to the parent reach the forks it created.
- Package 11 workspace_read_update_settings (draft): the update handler with `RegisterForkField` and `RegisterForkUpdateGuard`, the workspace object and `GET /workspaces/:slug`.
- Not dependencies: packages 49 and 45 implement the two narrow interfaces of this package (`SessionLinker` and the sandbox component) and register with them; package 17 copies tracking and version refs into the fork's repository; package 16 extends, expires and removes the forks created here.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires: after 7 days by default, or 24 hours after all its changes have landed or been abandoned.
- **Parent**: The repository workspace a fork was created from.
- **Base branch**: The parent branch a fork was taken from; the fork's `default_branch`.
- **Fork point**: The base branch and the parent's head of it when the fork was created.
- **Tracking branch**: In a fork, a branch that existed in the parent at fork time. It is read-only in the fork and always equals the parent's branch.
- **Own branch**: A branch created in a fork. It belongs to the fork alone and is not visible in the parent.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Path-scoped token**: A PAT whose writes are limited to files matching a list of globs.
- **Sandbox**: An isolated environment in which an agent runs, attached to a workspace (normally a task fork) and started with it checked out.
- **Session**: An agent session: who ran, on which workspace, with what token usage, and which changes it produced.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Fork creation in one call

**Rationale:** An agent starts work with one request and needs no second call to learn where its fork is or when it ends.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a caller with read access to a `ready` repository workspace sends `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/forks` with a valid body, THE parleyd SHALL create the fork synchronously as a workspace with slug `<parent slug>--<name>`, `kind` `fork`, `status` `ready`, `workspace_mode` `standard`, the caller as `owner_id`, the parent's `org_id`, `parent_slug` the parent, `display_name` the slug, `description` empty, and `git_url`, `origin_head_sha`, `upstream_url`, `integration_branch` and `upstream_head_sha` null
   → HTTP 201 with body `{workspace, remote}`; `workspace` is the fork's workspace object with `access` `owner` and `head_sha` equal to the parent's head of the base branch; `remote` equals `workspace.hub_url`, and is null when `[server].external_url` is empty; `token` and `sandbox` are absent when not requested; a `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<fork slug>` sent next answers 200
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: `[server].external_url` is `https://hub.test`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_AnswersReadyFork: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/forks', {name: 'task1'}) as the owner; assert r.status == 201; w = r.json.workspace; assert w.slug == 'demo--task1' and w.kind == 'fork' and w.status == 'ready' and w.workspace_mode == 'standard' and w.parent_slug == 'demo' and w.org_id == org('acme').id and w.owner_id == owner.id and w.access == 'owner' and w.git_url == null and w.display_name == 'demo--task1'; assert w.head_sha == git(demo, 'rev-parse main'); assert r.json.remote == w.hub_url == 'https://hub.test/git/acme/demo--task1.git'; assert 'token' not in r.json and 'sandbox' not in r.json; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--task1').status == 200; a second sub-test with external_url '' asserts r.json.remote == null; a third with a carry-patch parent asserts w.workspace_mode == 'standard' and w.upstream_url == null
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the request has no body, or a body `{}`, or a body whose members are null, or a body with members this route does not define, THE parleyd SHALL treat a null member as absent and apply the defaults: a generated `name` of 8 characters from lower-case letters and digits, `ref` the parent's default branch, `ttl` `[forks].default_ttl`, `auto_change` true, `purpose` null and `session_id` null, and ignore the undefined members
   → HTTP 201; `workspace.slug` matches `^demo--[a-z0-9]{8}$`; `workspace.default_branch` is the parent's default branch; `workspace.auto_change` is true; `workspace.purpose` and `workspace.session_id` are null; `workspace.expires_at` is `created_at` plus `[forks].default_ttl`
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: a fixed clock; `[forks].default_ttl` `7d`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_Defaults, a table over the bodies {absent, '{}', '{"colour":"red"}', '{"name":null,"ref":null,"ttl":null,"auto_change":null,"token":null,"purpose":null,"session_id":null,"sandbox":null}'}: r = post(...); assert r.status == 201; assert regexp('^demo--[a-z0-9]{8}$').match(w.slug); assert w.default_branch == 'main' and w.auto_change == true and w.purpose == null and w.session_id == null; assert w.expires_at == clock.now + 7d; assert 'token' not in r.json and 'sandbox' not in r.json
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN the caller is a member of the parent's organization who is not the parent's owner, or presents a PAT bound to the parent, THE parleyd SHALL create the fork with that caller's user as its owner, in the parent's organization
   → HTTP 201; `workspace.owner_id` is the caller's user id; `workspace.org_id` is the parent's; `workspace.access` is `owner`; the same member's `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/demo` still answers 403 `forbidden`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: the real access component and binding guard are installed
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_MemberOwnsFork, a table over the callers {member of acme with an API key, the owner with a PAT bound to 'demo' holding workspaces:write}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/forks', {}) as caller; assert r.status == 201; assert w.owner_id == caller.user and w.org_id == org('acme').id and w.access == 'owner'; for the member also assert patch('/api/v1/workspaces/demo', {description: 'x'}).status == 403
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN the body's `ref` names a branch of the parent, THE parleyd SHALL record that branch as the fork's base branch and `default_branch`, and record `fork_point` as `{ref, sha}` with the 40-character id of the parent's head of that branch at creation
   → HTTP 201; `workspace.default_branch` equals `ref`; `workspace.fork_point` equals `{ref: <ref>, sha: <parent head of ref at creation>}`; `workspace.head_sha` equals `fork_point.sha` at creation
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_ForkPoint: r = post(..., {ref: 'release'}); assert w.default_branch == 'release'; assert w.fork_point == {ref: 'release', sha: git(demo, 'rev-parse release')}; assert len(w.fork_point.sha) == 40; assert w.head_sha == w.fork_point.sha
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] WHEN the body's `ttl` is a duration of at least 5 minutes and at most `[forks].max_ttl`, THE parleyd SHALL set `expires_at` to the creation time plus `ttl`
   → HTTP 201; `workspace.expires_at` minus `workspace.created_at` equals `ttl`, for `5m`, `90m`, `24h` and a `ttl` equal to `[forks].max_ttl`
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: a fixed clock
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_TTL, a table over ttl {'5m', '90m', '24h', '30d'} with max_ttl '30d': r = post(..., {ttl}); assert r.status == 201; assert parse(w.expires_at) - parse(w.created_at) == duration(ttl)
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] WHEN a fork is created, THE parleyd SHALL write one hub event `parley.workspace.fork` in the same transaction as the fork, with the caller as actor, `workspace` and `resource_id` the fork's slug, the fork's `session_id` when it has one, and metadata `parent_slug`, `fork_point`, `expires_at`, `auto_change`, `purpose` and, when a token was minted, `token_id`
   → the event log holds exactly one `parley.workspace.fork` event for the fork with those members; metadata has no `token_id` when no token was requested and never a token value; a refused request adds no event
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: the real event log
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_EmitsForkEvent: post(..., {name: 'e1', purpose: 'fix loader'}); ev = events(type 'parley.workspace.fork'); assert len(ev) == 1; assert ev[0].workspace == 'demo--e1' and ev[0].resource_id == 'demo--e1' and ev[0].actor == owner; assert ev[0].metadata == {parent_slug: 'demo', fork_point: w.fork_point, expires_at: w.expires_at, auto_change: true, purpose: 'fix loader'}; post(..., {name: 'e2', token: {permissions: ['git:read']}}); assert events()[1].metadata.token_id == r.json.token.token_id and the raw event text does not contain r.json.token.token; post(..., {name: 'BAD'}); assert len(events(type 'parley.workspace.fork')) == 2
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] WHEN a request repeats an earlier successful fork creation with the same `Idempotency-Key`, caller and body within 24 hours, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the recorded response without the member `token.token`, and create nothing
   → HTTP 200 with the original body except that `token.token` is absent; the parent has one fork and the caller one token from the two requests
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: the idempotency middleware of the server is installed
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_IdempotentReplayOmitsSecret: body = {name: 'idem', token: {permissions: ['git:read']}}; a = post(..., body, header Idempotency-Key 'k1'); b = post(..., body, header Idempotency-Key 'k1'); assert a.status == 201 and b.status == 200; assert a.json.token.token != ''; assert 'token' not in b.json.token; assert b.json.workspace == a.json.workspace and b.json.token.token_id == a.json.token.token_id; assert count(forks of demo) == 1 and count(tokens bound to 'demo--idem') == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] IF a generated fork name is already in use for the parent, THEN THE parleyd SHALL generate another name, at most 8 times in all, and create the fork under the first free one
   → HTTP 201 with a slug different from every existing fork's; the caller never receives 409 for a name it did not give; when all 8 generated names are in use the answer is HTTP 500 with `error_type` `internal` and nothing is created
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_GeneratedNameCollision: with the name generator stubbed to return 'aaaaaaaa', 'aaaaaaaa', 'bbbbbbbb' and a fork 'demo--aaaaaaaa' present: r = post(..., {}); assert r.status == 201 and w.slug == 'demo--bbbbbbbb'; with the generator stubbed to always return 'aaaaaaaa': r = post(..., {}); assert r.status == 500 and r.json.error.error_type == 'internal'; assert generator.calls == 8; assert count(forks of demo) == 2
   ```

### REQ-2: Refusals of fork creation

**Rationale:** A caller must be able to tell from the status and the error type alone why no fork was made, and a refusal must leave nothing to clean up.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] IF the caller of `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/forks` is the admin token, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse at the access step, before reading the body, because a fork needs a user as owner
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden`, for a valid and for an invalid body; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: `unchanged(parent)` asserts: the count of fork records of the parent, the entries of the repository directory beside the parent's copy, the count of tokens and the count of events are what they were before the request
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesAdminToken, a table over the bodies {'{}', '{"name":"BAD"}', 'not json'}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/forks', body) with the admin token; assert r.status == 403 and r.json.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; assert unchanged(demo)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the body is not a JSON object, or `name` breaks the fork-name rule, or `ref` is not a non-empty string, or `ttl` is not a duration or is shorter than 5 minutes or longer than `[forks].max_ttl`, or `auto_change` is not a boolean, or `purpose` is not a string or exceeds 1024 characters, or `token` or `sandbox` is not an object, or `session_id` is not a UUID, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: `[forks].max_ttl` `30d`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesInvalidBody, a table over the bodies {'[]', '"x"', {name: ''}, {name: 'a'*33}, {name: 'Task'}, {name: '-a'}, {name: 'a-'}, {name: 'a--b'}, {name: 7}, {ref: ''}, {ref: 5}, {ttl: '4m'}, {ttl: '31d'} with max_ttl 30d, {ttl: '0m'}, {ttl: '90s'}, {ttl: '1.5h'}, {ttl: 60}, {auto_change: 'yes'}, {auto_change: 1}, {purpose: 'x'*1025}, {purpose: 3}, {token: 'git:read'}, {sandbox: []}, {session_id: 'not-a-uuid'}}: r = post(...); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert unchanged(demo); and the accepted boundaries {name: 'a'}, {name: 'a'*32}, {purpose: 'x'*1024} answer 201
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF the workspace named by `:slug` is itself a fork, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `not_supported_on_fork`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesForkOfFork: post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/forks', {name: 'f1'}); r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--f1/forks', {}); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'not_supported_on_fork'; assert count(all forks) == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF the parent is not `ready`, or a reclone, archive or delete is running on it, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request by the parent's state
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_busy` for `pending`, `cloning` and a set maintenance marker, `workspace_not_ready` for `failed`, and `workspace_archived` for `archived`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesByParentState, a table {pending: workspace_busy, cloning: workspace_busy, ready with the maintenance marker set: workspace_busy, failed: workspace_not_ready, archived: workspace_archived}: set the parent's state in the store; r = post(..., {}); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == want; assert unchanged(demo)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF `ref` does not name a branch of the parent, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request, also when `ref` names a tag or is a commit id of the parent
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `fork_ref_not_found`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesUnknownRef, a table over ref {'nope', 'v1' (a tag), 'refs/heads/main', the 40-character id of main's head, 'refs/tags/v1'}: r = post(..., {ref}); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'fork_ref_not_found'; assert unchanged(demo)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] IF the given `name` is already the name of a fork of the parent, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request; of several concurrent requests with the same `name`, create exactly one fork
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `conflict`; the existing fork is unchanged; of 8 concurrent requests with one `name`, exactly one answers 201 and seven answer 409 `conflict`, and one fork record and one repository directory exist for the name
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesNameInUse: post(..., {name: 'dup'}); r = post(..., {name: 'dup'}); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == 'conflict'; then 8 goroutines post {name: 'race'} at once: assert count(status == 201) == 1 and count(status == 409) == 7; assert count(fork records named 'demo--race') == 1 and the fork's repository opens with git
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] IF the parent already has `[forks].max_per_workspace` forks, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request, counting only forks that exist, and never let concurrent requests bring the parent above the limit
   → HTTP 429 with `error_type` `fork_limit_reached`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added; after one fork's record is removed the next request answers 201; of 6 concurrent requests against a parent with 1 free place, exactly one answers 201
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: `[forks].max_per_workspace` 3; a second `ready` workspace `other`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesAtForkLimit: with max_per_workspace 3: three posts answer 201; r = post(..., {}); assert r.status == 429 and r.json.error.error_type == 'fork_limit_reached'; assert unchanged(demo); remove one fork record through the store; assert post(..., {}).status == 201; remove one again; 6 goroutines post at once: assert count(status == 201) == 1 and count(status == 429) == 5; assert count(forks of demo) == 3; forks of another parent 'other' do not count: post('/api/v1/workspaces/other/forks', {}).status == 201
   ```
1. [REQ-2.8] IF a request fails more than one check, THEN THE parleyd SHALL answer by the first failing check in this order: caller is the admin token; body values; session link; parent is a fork; parent state; `ref`; fork limit; name in use; token refusal; sandbox refusal
   → the status and `error_type` are those of the earliest failing check of that order, for each adjacent pair of checks
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: a session linker stub that refuses, and a sandbox component stub that refuses with 422 `credential_missing`
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_refuse_test.go, TestCreate_RefusalOrder, a table of requests that fail two adjacent checks with the expected winner: {admin token + name 'BAD': 403 forbidden; name 'BAD' + unknown session: 400 invalid_request; unknown session + parent is a fork: 400 unknown_session; parent is a fork + (its parent archived): 400 not_supported_on_fork; parent archived + ref 'nope': 409 workspace_archived; ref 'nope' + limit reached: 400 fork_ref_not_found; limit reached + name in use: 429 fork_limit_reached; name in use + token with an unregistered scope: 409 conflict; token with an unregistered scope + refusing sandbox component: 400 invalid_request}: assert (r.status, r.json.error.error_type) == want
   ```

### REQ-3: A token minted with the fork

**Rationale:** An orchestrator hands an untrusted agent a credential that works on one fork only, without a second call in which the fork exists unprotected.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN the body has a `token` object with a non-empty `permissions` list of registered scopes, THE parleyd SHALL create, in the same transaction as the fork, a PAT owned by the caller and bound to the fork, with `name` defaulting to `fork:<fork slug>`, the given `permissions` and `paths`, and `expires_at` equal to the creation time plus `expires`, or null without `expires`
   → HTTP 201 whose `token` member is the token object with `workspace` the fork's slug, `user_id` the caller, `revoked_at` null and the secret in `token.token`; that secret authenticates `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<fork slug>` with 200 and gets 404 `not_found` on another workspace the caller owns; no later response of any route carries the secret
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: the real minting component and binding guard; a fixed clock; a second workspace `other` of the same owner
   ```
   in internal/fork/token_test.go, TestCreate_MintsBoundToken: r = post(..., {name: 't1', token: {permissions: ['git:read', 'workspaces:read'], paths: ['src/**']}}); t = r.json.token; assert t.workspace == 'demo--t1' and t.name == 'fork:demo--t1' and t.user_id == owner.id and t.permissions == ['git:read', 'workspaces:read'] and t.paths == ['src/**'] and t.expires_at == null and t.revoked_at == null and t.token startswith 'parley_pat_'; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--t1', bearer t.token).status == 200; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/other', bearer t.token).status == 404; the list of tokens bound to the fork shows t.token_id and no member 'token'; a second sub-test with {token: {name: 'ci', permissions: ['git:read'], expires: '2h'}} asserts t.name == 'ci' and t.expires_at == clock.now + 2h
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF the `token` object has no `permissions`, an empty `permissions`, an unregistered scope, an invalid `paths` glob, an `expires` that is not a duration, or a `name` that is not a string, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and create neither the token nor the fork
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: the real minting component
   ```
   in internal/fork/token_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesInvalidToken, a table over token {{}, {permissions: []}, {permissions: 'git:read'}, {permissions: ['no:such']}, {permissions: ['git:read'], paths: ['/abs']}, {permissions: ['git:read'], expires: 'soon'}, {permissions: ['git:read'], expires: '0h'}, {permissions: ['git:read'], name: 5}}: r = post(..., {name: 'bad', token}); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert unchanged(demo)
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF the caller authenticates with a PAT and the body has `token`, and the caller's PAT lacks `tokens:manage`, or does not itself hold a requested scope, or is path-limited while the request has no `paths` or a glob that none of the caller's globs covers, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and create neither the token nor the fork
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added; the same PAT with a body without `token` answers 201
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: the real minting component with the subset rule
   ```

   → a PAT bound to the parent gets HTTP 200 on `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>` of a fork it created and HTTP 404 `not_found` on a fork of the same parent created with another credential of the same user

### REQ-4: Session link and sandbox with the fork

**Rationale:** A fork is attributed to the agent session that asked for it, and an agent that asks for a sandbox never ends up with a fork it cannot run in.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN the body's `session_id` is a UUID that the session-linking rule accepts for the caller and the parent, THE parleyd SHALL store the id on the fork, carry it on the fork's events and record the link of the fork to the session through the linker's record operation inside the fork's creation transaction
   → HTTP 201 with `workspace.session_id` equal to the id; the `parley.workspace.fork` event carries the same `session_id`; the linker's check was asked once with the session id, the caller and the parent's slug, and its record was called once, with the fork's open transaction, the session id, the parent's slug and the fork's slug
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/session_test.go, TestCreate_LinksSession: sid = uuid(); linker = stub accepting (sid, owner, 'demo'); r = post(..., {session_id: sid}); assert r.status == 201 and w.session_id == sid; assert events(type 'parley.workspace.fork')[0].session_id == sid; assert linker.checks == [(sid, owner, 'demo')]; assert linker.records == [(sid, 'demo', w.slug)] and that the marker row the stub's record wrote through the transaction it was given is committed with the fork; a second sub-test whose record returns an error asserts 500 with error_type 'internal' and unchanged(demo)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF the body's `session_id` is a UUID that the session-linking rule refuses, or the hub has no session component, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `unknown_session`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/fork/session_test.go, TestCreate_RefusesUnknownSession, a table over the linkers {stub refusing every id, none wired}: r = post(..., {session_id: uuid()}); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'unknown_session'; assert unchanged(demo)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN the body has a `sandbox` object and the sandbox component accepts it, THE parleyd SHALL call the sandbox component once, inside the fork's transaction and after the fork's record, token and repository exist, with the caller, the fork, the `sandbox` object as received and the fork's `session_id` and `purpose` as defaults, and return the component's sandbox object
   → HTTP 201 with body `{workspace, remote, sandbox}` where `sandbox` is the component's object unchanged; the fork exists with `status` `ready`
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: a session linker stub that accepts
   ```
   in internal/fork/sandbox_test.go, TestCreate_PassesSandboxThrough: comp = stub returning {id: 'sbx_1', state: 'provisioning'}; r = post(..., {name: 's1', purpose: 'p', session_id: sid, sandbox: {profile: 'default', command: ['make', 'test'], extra: 1}}); assert r.status == 201 and r.json.sandbox == {id: 'sbx_1', state: 'provisioning'} and w.status == 'ready'; assert comp.calls == 1; c = comp.last; assert c.caller == owner and c.fork.slug == 'demo--s1' and c.raw == the bytes of the sandbox member and c.default_session_id == sid and c.default_purpose == 'p'; assert c.fork_record_visible_in_tx and c.fork_repository_exists
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] IF the body has a `sandbox` object and the sandbox component refuses it, THEN THE parleyd SHALL create no fork and answer with the component's error
   → the response has the status, `error_type` and extra members of the component's error unchanged; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added, also when the same request asked for a token
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`

   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] IF the body has a `sandbox` object and the hub has no sandbox component, THEN THE parleyd SHALL create no fork
   → HTTP 404 with `error_type` `sandboxes_disabled`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added
   Check: unit

### REQ-5: No copy of history

**Rationale:** A fork of a very large repository must be as quick and as small as a fork of an empty one.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE parleyd SHALL for any parent repository, create a fork's repository without writing an object or a pack into it and without changing the parent's repository
   → after creation `git count-objects -v` in the fork's repository reports `count: 0` and `in-pack: 0`; the parent's refs and object counts are what they were before
   Check: integration
   - setup: a bare parent repository made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()` holding 3 commits on `main`, branch `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/fork_test.go, TestCreateFork_CopiesNothing, a table over parents {1 commit, 300 commits in a pack}: before = (git(parent, 'for-each-ref'), git(parent, 'count-objects -v')); CreateFork(parentDir, forkDir); c = git(forkDir, 'count-objects -v'); assert c.count == 0 and c['in-pack'] == 0; assert (git(parent, 'for-each-ref'), git(parent, 'count-objects -v')) == before; assert git(forkDir, 'rev-parse --is-bare-repository') == 'true'
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any commit reachable from a branch or tag of the parent, make it readable through the fork's repository from the moment the fork exists, including commits the parent receives after the fork was created
   → `git cat-file -e <id>` in the fork's repository succeeds for the heads of the parent's branches and tags and for a commit added to the parent afterwards; `git log <parent head>` in the fork lists the parent's full history
   Check: integration
   - setup: a bare parent repository made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()` holding 3 commits on `main`, branch `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/fork_test.go, TestCreateFork_SharesHistory: CreateFork(parentDir, forkDir); for id in {rev-parse main, release, v1 in the parent}: assert git(forkDir, 'cat-file -e ' + id) exits 0; assert count(git(forkDir, 'rev-list ' + mainHead)) == 3; n = commit a new file on main in the parent; assert git(forkDir, 'cat-file -e ' + n) exits 0
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any branch and commit written to a fork, store them in the fork's repository alone
   → after a commit is pushed to a new branch of the fork, the parent's ref list is unchanged, `git cat-file -e <new id>` fails in the parent, and the fork's object count is the number of objects pushed
   Check: integration
   - setup: a bare parent repository made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()` holding 3 commits on `main`, branch `release` and tag `v1`
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/fork_test.go, TestCreateFork_OwnWorkStaysInFork: CreateFork(parentDir, forkDir); refs = git(parent, 'for-each-ref'); clone the fork's directory into a working tree, commit one changed file on branch 'task' and push it to forkDir; id = the new commit; assert git(forkDir, 'rev-parse refs/heads/task') == id; assert git(parent, 'for-each-ref') == refs; assert git(parent, 'cat-file -e ' + id) exits non-zero; assert git(forkDir, 'count-objects -v').count == 3
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] IF the fork's repository cannot be created, or the fork's transaction fails after the repository was created, THEN THE parleyd SHALL remove what was made and answer with an internal error; and when a directory without a fork record is found at a new fork's place, discard it and create the fork
   → HTTP 500 with `error_type` `internal`; no fork record, no repository directory, no token and no event are added; a request for a name whose directory is a leftover answers 201 with a repository that holds no object
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub built in-process with a real store and a real `git`; a `ready` repository workspace `demo` owned by a developer in organization `acme`, with branches `main` (default) and `release` and tag `v1`
   - setup: fault injection on the repository creator, the store and the event sink
   ```
   in internal/fork/create_test.go, TestCreate_CleansUpOnFailure, a table over the faults {repository creation returns an error, the store's commit returns an error, the event sink returns an error}: r = post(..., {name: 'x1'}); assert r.status == 500 and r.json.error.error_type == 'internal'; assert unchanged(demo) and not exists(forkDir('demo--x1')); then with no fault and a directory forkDir('demo--x2') holding a stray file: r = post(..., {name: 'x2'}); assert r.status == 201; assert the stray file is gone and git(forkDir('demo--x2'), 'count-objects -v').count == 0
   ```

### REQ-6: The fork's refs

**Rationale:** An agent sees the parent as it is now without a sync call, and cannot move what belongs to the parent.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] THE parleyd SHALL for any fork, show in its ref view every branch the parent had when the fork was created as a tracking branch whose head is the parent's current head of the branch of the same name
   → the view lists `main` and `release` with `tracking` true at the parent's heads; after the parent's `main` moves, the next read of the view shows `main` at the new head with no other call
   Check: integration
   - setup: a parent with branches `main`, `release` and tag `v1`, and a fork `demo--f` of it taken from `main`, both on real repositories and a real store
   ```
   in internal/fork/refs_test.go, TestRefs_TrackingFollowsParent: v = Refs('demo--f'); assert v.branches == [{name: 'main', sha: head(parent, 'main'), tracking: true}, {name: 'release', sha: head(parent, 'release'), tracking: true}]; n = commit on main in the parent; v = Refs('demo--f'); assert v.branch('main').sha == n; assert git(forkDir, 'for-each-ref refs/heads') == ''
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN the parent's branch of a tracking branch's name is deleted, or the parent gains a branch after the fork was created, THE parleyd SHALL leave the deleted branch out of the fork's ref view until the parent has a branch of that name again, and never show the later branch
   → after `release` is deleted in the parent the view has no `release`; after it is created again the view shows it at the parent's head with `tracking` true; a branch `later` created in the parent after the fork never appears in the view
   Check: integration
   - setup: a parent with branches `main`, `release` and tag `v1`, and a fork `demo--f` of it taken from `main`, both on real repositories and a real store
   ```
   in internal/fork/refs_test.go, TestRefs_DeletedAndLaterBranches: git(parent, 'branch -D release'); assert Refs('demo--f').branch('release') == none; git(parent, 'branch release main'); b = Refs('demo--f').branch('release'); assert b.tracking and b.sha == head(parent, 'main'); git(parent, 'branch later main'); assert Refs('demo--f').branch('later') == none
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any fork, show in its ref view the tags the parent had when the fork was created, each at the parent's current target of the tag of the same name, and no tag the parent gained later
   → the view's tags are exactly `v1` at the parent's target; a tag `v2` created in the parent afterwards is absent; after `v1` is deleted in the parent it is absent
   Check: integration
   - setup: a parent with branches `main`, `release` and tag `v1`, and a fork `demo--f` of it taken from `main`, both on real repositories and a real store
   ```
   in internal/fork/refs_test.go, TestRefs_Tags: assert Refs('demo--f').tags == [{name: 'v1', sha: git(parent, 'rev-parse v1')}]; git(parent, 'tag v2 main'); assert Refs('demo--f').tag('v2') == none; git(parent, 'tag -d v1'); assert Refs('demo--f').tags == []
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any branch created in the fork, show it in the fork's ref view as an own branch at its head in the fork, also when the parent later creates a branch of the same name
   → the view lists the own branch with `tracking` false at the fork's head; after the parent creates a branch of that name at another commit, the view still shows one branch of that name, `tracking` false, at the fork's head
   Check: integration
   - setup: a parent with branches `main`, `release` and tag `v1`, and a fork `demo--f` of it taken from `main`, both on real repositories and a real store
   ```
   in internal/fork/refs_test.go, TestRefs_OwnBranches: id = push a commit to branch 'task' of the fork; assert Refs('demo--f').branch('task') == {name: 'task', sha: id, tracking: false}; git(parent, 'branch task main'); bs = Refs('demo--f').branches where name == 'task'; assert len(bs) == 1 and bs[0].sha == id and bs[0].tracking == false; assert branch 'task' was not in the parent's refs before the parent created it; then git(fork repository, 'update-ref refs/heads/release <parent head of release>') and 'update-ref refs/parley/changes/7/1 <id>', as the copy package 17 makes before serving a fork; assert Refs('demo--f').branches where name == 'release' is one entry with tracking true, and that the entries with tracking false are exactly ['task']
   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] IF a component asks whether a branch of a fork may be created, moved or deleted and the branch's name is the name of one of the fork's tracking branches, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse, also while the parent has no branch of that name
   → the write check returns an error with HTTP status 403 and `error_type` `tracking_branch`; for any other branch name of a fork, and for every branch of a repository workspace, it returns no error
   Check: unit
   - setup: a parent with branches `main`, `release` and tag `v1`, and a fork `demo--f` of it taken from `main`, both on real repositories and a real store
   ```
   in internal/fork/refs_test.go, TestCheckBranchWrite, a table over (workspace, branch, want) {('demo--f', 'main', tracking_branch), ('demo--f', 'release', tracking_branch), ('demo--f', 'release' after the parent deleted it, tracking_branch), ('demo--f', 'task', ok), ('demo--f', 'later' created in the parent after the fork, ok), ('demo', 'main', ok)}: err = CheckBranchWrite(workspace, branch); if want == ok: assert err == nil; else: assert err.status == 403 and err.error_type == 'tracking_branch'
   ```
1. [REQ-6.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any read of a fork, report `head_sha` as the parent's current head of the fork's base branch, or null when the parent has no such branch, and report `fork_point.sha` as recorded at creation
   → after the parent's base branch moves, `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<fork slug>` shows the new id in `head_sha` and the creation-time id in `fork_point.sha`; after the base branch is deleted in the parent it shows `head_sha` null and still answers 200
   Check: integration
   - setup: a parent with branches `main`, `release` and tag `v1`, and a fork `demo--f` of it taken from `main`, both on real repositories and a real store
   - setup: the workspace read route is served, or the workspace object is rendered directly when that route is not present yet
   ```
   in internal/fork/refs_test.go, TestHeadSHA_FollowsBaseBranch: p = fork.fork_point.sha; n = commit on main in the parent; assert HeadSHA('demo--f') == n; w = get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--f').json; assert w.head_sha == n and w.fork_point.sha == p; move main aside and delete it in the parent; r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--f'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.head_sha == null and r.json.fork_point.sha == p
   ```

### REQ-7: A fork follows its parent's status

**Rationale:** Archiving a workspace must stop the work in its forks without losing what they hold, and the owner changes what a fork is for without making a new one.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] IF a component asks whether a fork may be written while the fork's parent is `archived`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the write and allow a read
   → the parent-state check returns, for a write, an error with HTTP status 409 and `error_type` `parent_archived`, and for a read no error; with a `ready` parent it returns no error for both; for a repository workspace it returns no error
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fork `demo--f` of `demo` in a real store
   ```
   in internal/fork/guard_test.go, TestCheckParentState, a table over (parent state, use, want) {(ready, read, ok), (ready, write, ok), (archived, read, ok), (archived, write, 409 parent_archived), (pending, read, 409 workspace_busy), (pending, write, 409 workspace_busy), (cloning, read, 409 workspace_busy), (cloning, write, 409 workspace_busy), (ready with the maintenance marker set, read, 409 workspace_busy), (ready with the maintenance marker set, write, 409 workspace_busy), (failed, read, 409 workspace_not_ready), (failed, write, 409 workspace_not_ready)}: set the parent's state in the store; err = CheckParentState('demo--f', use); assert (err.status, err.error_type) == want or err == nil; and CheckParentState('demo', write) == nil
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF a component asks whether a fork may be read or written while the fork's parent is `pending`, `cloning` or `failed`, or an archive or delete is running on the parent, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse both uses
   → the parent-state check returns an error with HTTP status 409 and `error_type` `workspace_busy` for `pending`, `cloning` and a set maintenance marker, and `workspace_not_ready` for `failed`
   Check: same as REQ-7.1
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN a caller with write access to a fork sends `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/<fork slug>` with `purpose` (a string of at most 1024 characters, or null) or `auto_change` (a boolean) while the parent is `ready`, THE parleyd SHALL store the given values, clearing `purpose` on null, and record `parley.workspace.update` with the given names in `metadata.fields` and the fork's `session_id`
   → HTTP 200 with the fork's workspace object showing the new values and an `updated_at` not earlier than before; fields not given are unchanged; the event's `metadata.fields` lists `purpose` and `auto_change` in that order after any other given name, and `metadata.parent_slug` is the parent
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub in-process with the update route of the workspace component; a fork `demo--f` created with a session id by an org member
   ```
   in internal/fork/update_test.go, TestUpdate_ForkFields: r = patch('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--f', {auto_change: false, purpose: 'new aim'}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.auto_change == false and r.json.purpose == 'new aim' and r.json.expires_at == before.expires_at; ev = last event; assert ev.type == 'parley.workspace.update' and ev.metadata.fields == ['purpose', 'auto_change'] and ev.metadata.parent_slug == 'demo' and ev.session_id == fork.session_id; r = patch(..., {purpose: null}); assert r.json.purpose == null and r.json.auto_change == false; r = patch(..., {description: 'd', purpose: 'p'}); assert last event.metadata.fields == ['description', 'purpose']; as the parent's owner patch(..., {purpose: 'by parent owner'}).status == 200; as a member who is not the fork's owner patch(...).status == 403
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] IF an update of a fork gives `auto_change` as null or as a value that is not a boolean, or `purpose` as a value that is not a string or null or as a string longer than 1024 characters, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the update and change nothing
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; the fork's record is unchanged and no event is recorded; a `purpose` of exactly 1024 characters answers 200
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub in-process with the update route of the workspace component; a fork `demo--f`
   ```
   in internal/fork/update_test.go, TestUpdate_RefusesInvalidForkFields, a table over the bodies {{auto_change: null}, {auto_change: 'no'}, {auto_change: 0}, {purpose: 7}, {purpose: 'x'*1025}, {purpose: 'ok', auto_change: 'no'}}: before = store.fork('demo--f'); n = count(events); r = patch('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--f', body); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert store.fork('demo--f') == before and count(events) == n; assert patch(..., {purpose: 'x'*1024}).status == 200
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] IF a caller with write access sends a valid `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/<fork slug>`, with whichever fields, while the fork's parent is `archived`, busy or `failed`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the update by the parent-state check for a write and change nothing
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `parent_archived` for an archived parent, `workspace_busy` for a `pending` or `cloning` parent or a set maintenance marker, `workspace_not_ready` for a `failed` parent; the fork's record is unchanged; `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<fork slug>` still answers 200 while the parent is archived
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub in-process with the update and read routes of the workspace component; a fork `demo--f`
   ```
   in internal/fork/update_test.go, TestUpdate_RefusedByParentState, a table over (parent state, want) {(archived, parent_archived), (pending, workspace_busy), (maintenance marker set, workspace_busy), (failed, workspace_not_ready)} and over the bodies {{purpose: 'p'}, {auto_change: false}, {display_name: 'n'}}: set the parent's state in the store; r = patch('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--f', body); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == want; assert store.fork('demo--f') == before; with the parent archived: assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo--f').status == 200; and an invalid body {auto_change: null} with an archived parent answers 400, validation before state
   ```

### REQ-8: Listing a workspace's forks

**Rationale:** An owner sees who works on their repository, and an orchestrator finds the forks of one run.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN a caller with read access to a workspace sends `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/forks`, with an API key or with a PAT that holds `workspaces:read` or `workspaces:write`, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the forks of that workspace as workspace objects carrying the caller's `access`, ordered by `created_at` descending and then `slug` ascending, in pages by `limit` and `cursor`, whatever the parent's status
   → HTTP 200 with `{items, next_cursor}`; walking the pages returns every fork once in that order; `next_cursor` is null on the last page; each item has `kind` `fork`, `parent_slug` the workspace and `access` `owner` for the fork's owner and the parent's owner and `member` for other members; a PAT with neither scope gets 403 `insufficient_scope`; a caller with no read access gets 404 `not_found`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub in-process; `demo` with forks `demo--a` (by the owner, oldest), `demo--b` (by a member, with session S) and `demo--c` and `demo--d` (by the owner, created in the same second, newest); a fixed clock
   ```
   in internal/fork/list_test.go, TestList_OrderPagingAccess: r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/forks') as the owner; assert r.status == 200 and slugs(r.json.items) == ['demo--c', 'demo--d', 'demo--b', 'demo--a'] and r.json.next_cursor == null; assert every item.access == 'owner' and item.kind == 'fork' and item.parent_slug == 'demo'; p1 = get('...?limit=3'); p2 = get('...?limit=3&cursor=' + p1.json.next_cursor); assert slugs(p1.items + p2.items) == the same four and p2.json.next_cursor == null; as the member: access is 'owner' on 'demo--b' and 'member' on the others; with a PAT holding only workspaces:write: status 200; with a PAT holding only git:read: 403 insufficient_scope; as a stranger: 404 not_found; with the parent archived in the store: status 200 with the same four
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN the query has `owner=me` or `session_id=<UUID>`, THE parleyd SHALL keep only the forks whose owner is the caller's user, and only the forks created with that session; with both, keep the forks that satisfy both
   → HTTP 200; `owner=me` for the member lists `demo--b` only; `session_id=S` lists `demo--b` only; `owner=me&session_id=S` for the owner lists nothing; `owner=me` with the admin token lists nothing; a session id no fork carries lists nothing
   Check: unit
